label: Deployed page
subject: page
use: The change is merged and live
reaches: The page as everyone sees it

label: Toss
subject: page;file;data;fileset
use: A branch changed a page or its code
reaches: The branch's page, private repos too
misses: The tab's title, icon and history
trap: ?use= on the renderer crashes iPhone Safari
narrative: Any branch change to a page: its own shell, or lib/ and dist/ with the page untouched, since the toss hands the page its ref. Where the page and what it reads belong at different refs, add refs= (or ?lib=<ref>) to the renderer's query, never ?use=. With nothing selected, a web-tools page runs its own ref and any other repo's page runs main. It reaches the branch's real page file, shell and all; with refs= on the renderer, each repository, file or folder the page's code reads at a ref of its own (?lib=<ref> is the web-tools entry), including one changed library file over an otherwise unchanged build; and a routed toss's viewer page. With ?top, the page becomes the tab's own document, with the same inlining, fetch shim and selection: its title, icon, history and reload are the tab's, and its FAB is its own, at the Web Tools selection. It misses, in the default frame mode: anything the page does to the TOP-LEVEL document (title, favicon, history, navigation), and anything the SHELL contributes to the view: the FAB and the Alpine bundle come from the default branch whatever ref the address names, so a branch change to lib/alpineComponents/fab.js needs ?top; in both modes, a tossed page's relative images, CSS url(), import() and iframes, which load from the deployed site. ?top is not available with ?w= or for a payload, which keep the frame. On an iPhone it held for a walkthrough across two app tabs and a document (measured on the device, 2026-10-23). The @<ref> pins the SUBJECT, which is what carries the branch's lib into the framed page; never add ?use= to the shell, which on an iPhone kills Safari's web process when the shell is also hosting a frame (measured by matrix on the device, 2026-09-08; the mechanism is not yet established).

label: Merge preview
form: pages/toss-render.html?refs=owner/repo@<main sha>&refs=owner/repo@<branch sha>:<changed path>&…#gh=owner/repo@<main sha or branch sha>:<page>
subject: page;file
version: main at a pinned commit, with each file the branch changed read at the branch's commit
reaches: The branch's files over current main
narrative: A web-tools branch that lags main, previewed as it would merge. npm run showing offers it once main's renderer and build read path entries; composing versions by hand with refs= is always available. It reaches the tree a merge would produce, for the files the branch changed, when main changed none of them since the branch point and the branch removes or renames none; npm run showing checks both and offers it only then. It misses files a merge regenerates (dist/, the hook's whole generated files, the derived-csv catalogs), which are read at main and named; and, when the conditions fail, the merge itself: whole-file replacement would drop main's edits to a file both sides changed, so the script links the branch as it stands and says so. Not a merge preview when a file changed on both sides, or when the branch deletes or renames a file; the script refuses it then rather than claiming it. Past 20 changed files it steps aside for the branch as it stands.

label: Framing app
subject: page
use: The change sits in an app view
reaches: The app around the branch's page
misses: Headless screenshots, which come back empty
narrative: The repo's .web-tools.json names the app under showing.app, and the change is under a declared view's prefix or the app's own folder. No ?use=: the renderer is web-tools main and the ref belongs to the framed repo. A ?lib=<ref> on the renderer picks the Web Tools code, and the app hands it on to every view that names none of its own. It reaches the app carrying the branch's copy of the framed page, and the app's own files. It misses the framed page addressed on its own, which is the route the session store recorded as wrong most often; pixels, since the frame fetches on the viewer's token and a headless shot comes back empty.

label: Nested toss
subject: page
use: The change is the renderer itself
reaches: The renderer's routing, framing and rendering
misses: The tab's title, icon and history
narrative: The change IS toss-render. Address the branch's renderer, hand it the page as a trailing fragment. It reaches the renderer's own internals: routing, frame mounting, rendering, address parsing. It misses the top-level document, as a toss in its frame does; a nested shell is never the tab.

label: Data route
subject: file;data
use: A document or data file changed
reaches: Markdown rendered, CSV and JSON as tables
narrative: A document or data file changed on a branch, alone or beside a page. npm run showing prints it after any page links. It reaches a document or data file at the ref in the address, read by the data viewer (pages/data-view.html): Markdown as a preview, CSV and JSON as a table, every other mode one tap away; a trailing #frag reaches the viewer, so a look link rides on it. It misses a page, which this route reads as text rather than running: an .html file is addressed with #gh=.

label: Packed link
subject: page
reaches: The page itself, packed into the link
misses: Files the page loads by relative path
narrative: The reader has no token, or you want the bytes pinned into the link itself. It reaches any reader, no token, nothing hosted, and misses same-repo relative dependencies; only absolute-URL CDN deps resolve.

label: Claude artifact
subject: page
reaches: A self-contained copy of the page
narrative: The link will be opened in the Claude app AND the page can be baked self-contained. It reaches a reader in the Claude app, where the GitHub token may be absent, and misses anything needing the network: artifact CSP blocks every external request.

label: ?use= link
subject: page
reaches: Branch library code in the live page
trap: Old page markup around new code
narrative: Not picked for a new link: a toss at the branch shows the same lib/ or dist/ change and also reaches private repos. Links already handed over keep working. It reaches anything lib/ or dist/ does, including what it does to the tab itself, and misses the page's own inline shell: its markup, and any x-data defined in the file. Pages serves the page FILE from the default branch, so a shell change shows the old shell wrapped around new lib, silently and with nothing reporting the mismatch.

label: No link
subject: page
narrative: Send an inspected headless screenshot and say plainly that no link can show it. A page shell's change to its title, icon, history or navigation is not this row: python/showing.py links it as a toss with ?top. It misses everything: ?use= keeps the old shell, and ?top cannot help where the frame has to stay: the renderer's own effects on the tab (a nested shell is never the tab, and toss-render cannot render itself at the top), a forced width (?w=) and a carried payload.
